study_identification_part.si_4_title: Closing the life-cycle of normative modeling using federated hierarchical Bayesian regression

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study proposes a federated probabilistic framework using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) for normative modeling. This approach is compared with naive pooling, fixed-effect pooling, pooling after ComBat harmonization, and no-pooling. The HBR model is parametrized with a site-specific homoscedastic form for the variance in the main experiments, although the framework supports heteroscedastic noise.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we approach the problem of estimating a reference normative model across a massive population... To this end, we introduce a federated probabilistic framework using hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR)... we propose a partial pooling approach based on hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) as a possible solution for completing the life-cycle of normative modeling.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Kia2022.pdf.md: Abstract; Materials and methods / A solution: Partial-pooling using hierarchical Bayesian regression

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study models cortical thickness measures estimated by FreeSurfer over 148 cortical regions using the Destrieux atlas.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: In our analyses, we use cortical thickness measures estimated by Freesurfer version 5.3 or 6.0 over 148 cortical regions in the Destrieux atlas [57].
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Kia2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Experimental materials and setups / Datasets and preprocessing

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age is used as the primary covariate. Sex and Scanner (or site) are included as group-effects in the HBR model. In fixed-effect site modeling, scanner IDs are included as covariates.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: In all experimental configurations, we use only age as a covariate except for the fixed-effect site modeling in which, by definition, the one-hot encoding of scanner ids are also included in the covariates. We use sex as a group-effect in all estimated models. In the HBR case, the scanner is also included as a group-effect.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Kia2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Experimental materials and setups / Experiments
